title: EY built an ‘AI router’ to stop its own AI bills from spiralling

content_html:
EY has built what it calls an “AI router,” a system that steers each task to the cheapest model that can handle it, in an effort to keep its own soaring AI bills under control.

The tool, reported by Business Insider, is the Big Four firm’s answer to a problem now spreading across corporate IT: the cost of the tokens that AI consumes.The logic is simple arbitrage.

Not every request needs the most powerful, most expensive model, so a router sends easy work to a cheap one and reserves the pricey models for the hard problems, trimming the bill without obviously trimming the output.

EY has reason to watch the meter. The firm invests more than $1 billion a year in AI, runs a fleet of some 1,000 AI agents, and has seen its AI-related consulting revenue jump around 30%, a scale at which token costs stop being a rounding error, in a market where the most AI-obsessed firms spend thousands per employee a month.

Its own research shows the anxiety is widespread. In EY’s latest AI Pulse survey of 534 senior US business leaders, 82% said they were concerned about token-usage costs, and 98% of those using token-based tools said the costs had made them reconsider their strategy.

Yet most companies are flying blind. Only 64% of the firms surveyed said they actively monitor token usage with budgetary guardrails, which means a third are spending on AI without a clear meter, a recipe for the bill shocks that have hit the sector.

The mood has shifted from more to enough. EY’s global AI consulting leader, Dan Diasio, put it plainly: “‘AI saves time’ is no longer sufficient when costs mount and remain unclear,” a line that captures the turn from adoption at any price to value at a known one.

The token economics are genuinely strange. The price per token has collapsed as models get cheaper, yet enterprise AI bills have tripled, because agentic tools that run many steps consume far more tokens than a single chatbot prompt ever did.

That is the paradox a router is built for. If each task can be matched to the least costly model that still does the job, a company can keep using AI aggressively while stopping the total from ballooning, which is exactly what EY is trying to prove at its own scale.

It is not alone in the effort. The industry spent two years urging staff to use as much AI as possible, a fashion nicknamed tokenmaxxing, and is now swinging the other way, with firms from Atlassian to Amazon imposing budgets and controls.

For a consultancy, though, the router is also a product. EY sells AI advice to other companies, so a tool that visibly tames its own costs doubles as a demonstration, evidence that the firm can do for clients what it has done for itself.

The survey points the same way. Some 76% of leaders told EY that off-the-shelf software no longer meets their needs, and 91% now see building AI tools in-house as critical, a shift that favours firms selling the expertise to build them.

The catch is that in-house building is hard. Nearly three-quarters of the leaders EY surveyed said their own AI development was slowing progress, and a third flagged shadow-IT and governance risks, the messy reality behind the clean promise of a router.

What the story really marks is a change of question. The first phase of the AI boom asked whether a tool worked; the second, which EY’s router belongs to, asks what it costs, and whether the value justifies the meter.

EY’s answer, for now, is to build the meter itself. A firm that spends a billion dollars a year on AI has decided that the way to keep spending is to watch every token, which is less a retreat from AI than a sign of how much of it is now in use.

content_html_zh:
安永构建了所谓的“人工智能路由器”，该系统将每项任务引导至能够处理该任务的最便宜的模型，以努力控制其不断飙升的人工智能费用。

据 Business Insider 报道，该工具是四大公司针对目前整个企业 IT 中普遍存在的一个问题的答案：人工智能消耗的代币成本。其逻辑是简单的套利。

并非每个请求都需要最强大、最昂贵的模型，因此路由器将简单的工作发送给便宜的模型，并为困难的问题保留昂贵的模型，从而在不明显减少输出的情况下削减费用。

安永有理由关注仪表。 该公司每年在人工智能方面的投资超过 10 亿美元，运营着一支由约 1,000 名人工智能代理组成的团队，其与人工智能相关的咨询收入增长了 30% 左右，在这个最痴迷于人工智能的公司每个员工每月花费数千美元的市场中，代币成本不再是一个舍入误差。

它自己的研究表明焦虑很普遍。 在安永对 534 名美国高级商业领袖进行的最新 AI Pulse 调查中，82% 的人表示他们担心代币使用成本，而使用基于代币的工具的人中 98% 表示这些成本让他们重新考虑自己的策略。

然而大多数公司都在盲目行动。 只有 64% 的受访公司表示，他们通过预算护栏积极监控代币的使用情况，这意味着三分之一的公司在没有明确计量的情况下在人工智能上进行支出，这是该行业遭受账单冲击的原因之一。

心情已经从多转为够了。 安永全球人工智能咨询负责人丹·迪亚西奥 (Dan Diasio) 直言不讳地说：“当成本上升且仍不明确时，‘人工智能节省时间’就不再足够了”，这句话抓住了从以任何价格采用到以已知价格实现价值的转变。

代币经济学确实很奇怪。 随着模型变得更便宜，每个代币的价格已经暴跌，但企业人工智能费用却增加了两倍，因为运行许多步骤的代理工具比单个聊天机器人提示消耗的代币要多得多。

这就是路由器的诞生所面临的悖论。 如果每项任务都可以与仍能完成工作的成本最低的模型相匹配，那么公司就可以继续积极使用人工智能，同时阻止总数不断膨胀，这正是安永试图以自己的规模证明的事情。

它并不是唯一在努力的人。 该行业花了两年时间敦促员工尽可能多地使用人工智能，这种时尚被称为“tokenmaxxing”，但现在却转向了另一个方向，从 Atlassian 到亚马逊等公司都实施了预算和控制。

但对于咨询公司来说，路由器也是一种产品。 安永向其他公司出售人工智能建议，因此一种明显降低自身成本的工具可以兼作演示，证明该公司可以为客户做它自己所做的事情。

调查也表明了同样的观点。 约 76% 的领导者告诉安永，现成的软件不再满足他们的需求，91% 的领导者现在认为内部构建人工智能工具至关重要，这一转变有利于出售构建这些工具的专业知识的公司。

问题是内部建设很困难。 近四分之三接受安永调查的领导者表示，他们自己的人工智能开发进展正在放缓，三分之一的人指出了影子 IT 和治理风险，即路由器干净承诺背后的混乱现实。

这个故事真正标志着的是问题的改变。 人工智能热潮的第一阶段询问工具是否有效；第二个是 EY 的路由器所属的，询问其价格是多少，以及该价格是否合理。

安永目前的答案是自己建造电表。 一家每年在人工智能上花费 10 亿美元的公司决定，持续支出的方法是关注每一个代币，这与其说是对人工智能的撤退，不如说是人工智能目前使用量的标志。
